sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Supported formats and parser version
sections.what: Lists the file endings the app accepts and sets the parser version to 1.4.0.
sections.why: The version number lets cached results from an older reader be recognised and not reused after a change in stored structure.
sections.watch_out: The version must be raised whenever the stored database structure changes, or old cached results will come back.

sections.name: ingest_schedule
sections.title: Routing a file to its reader
sections.what: Checks the file ending, deletes any old database at the target path, then sends XER, P6 XML, XLSX, and CSV or TSV files to their matching readers. Unknown endings are refused with a message listing the supported types.
sections.why: One entry point keeps callers simple and keeps format decisions in one place.
sections.watch_out: The target database is deleted before parsing starts, so an earlier result at that path is lost even if the new parse fails.

summary: Routes each uploaded schedule file to the correct reader based on its file ending.
purpose: Gives the rest of the app one entry point for ingesting any supported schedule file.
why: Callers do not need to know which reader each format needs. The parser version number exists so old cached results are not reused after a change.
how: It checks the file ending against the supported list, deletes any old database at the target path, then calls the matching reader. Column mapping and default project name are passed only to the spreadsheet and text-table readers.
inputs: A source file path, a target database path, optional progress and cancel callbacks, an optional column mapping, and an optional default project name.
outputs: The ingestion report returned by the chosen reader.
risks: The target database is deleted before parsing, so an earlier result at that path is lost even if the new parse fails. The parser version must be raised whenever stored structure changes.
debug: If a file is refused, check its ending against the supported list. If an old result seems to come back, check whether the parser version was raised after a structure change.
